abrams-human-energy-1914.title: Human Energy
abrams-human-energy-1914.creator: Albert Abrams
abrams-human-energy-1914.description: Abrams' foundational statement of the electronic theory behind radionics ('Electronic Reactions of Abrams'), arguing diseases emit measurable electronic vibrations. Public domain (author d. 1924); HathiTrust PD Google-digitized scan.

arxiv-1911-09370.title: Energy consumption in compact integer vectors: A study case
arxiv-1911-09370.creator: JOSÉ FUENTES-SEPÚLVEDA 1, SUSANA LADRA 2
arxiv-1911-09370.description: Abstract In the field of algorithms and data structures analysis and design, most of the researchers focus only on the space/time trade-off, and little attention has been paid to energy consumption. Moreover, most of the efforts in the field of Green Computing have been devoted to hardware-related issues, being green software in its infancy.

arxiv-2106-01414.title: Normalization for Multimodal Type Theory
arxiv-2106-01414.creator: Daniel Gratzer
arxiv-2106-01414.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Daniel Gratzer. We consider the conversion problem for multimodal type theory ( MTT ) [ Gra+20 ] by characterizing the normal forms of the type theory and proving normalization ( Theorem 8.5 ). Normalization follows from a novel adaptation of Sterling’s Synthetic Tait Computability [ SH20 , Ste21 ] which generalizes the framework to accommodate a type theory with modalities and multiple modes.

arxiv-2206-12130.title: Computer based activity to understand proper acceleration using the Rindler observer
arxiv-2206-12130.creator: Sushil Kumar Singh, Gervit Kumar Trehan, Savinder Kaur
arxiv-2206-12130.description: Abstract Using elementary knowledge of Special Relativity, we design a computational classroom experiment in excel and python. Here, we show that any inertial observer ℬ \mathcal{B} with an arbitrary speed u ℬ u_{\mathcal{B}} is associated with a unique event E {E} along the worldline of Rindler observer ℛ \mathcal{R} .

arxiv-2306-03304.title: Plasma flows during the ablation stage of an over-massed pulsed-power-driven exploding planar wire array
arxiv-2306-03304.creator: R. Datta, J. Angel, J.B. Greenly, S.N. Bland, J.P. Chittenden, E. S. Lavine, W. M. Potter, D. Robinson, T. W. O. Varnish, E. Wong, D. A. Hammer, B.R. Kusse, J.D. Hare*
arxiv-2306-03304.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by R. Datta, J. Angel, J.B. Greenly, S.N. Bland, J.P. Chittenden, E. S. Lavine, W. M. Potter, D. Robinson, T. W. O. Varnish, E. Wong, D. A. Hammer, B.R. Kusse, J.D. Hare*. We characterize the plasma flows generated during the ablation stage of an over-massed exploding planar wire array, fielded on the COBRA pulsed-power facility (1 MA peak current, 250 ns rise time).

arxiv-2409-18205.title: Bridging OOD Detection and Generalization: A Graph-Theoretic View
arxiv-2409-18205.creator: Han Wang, Yixuan Li
arxiv-2409-18205.description: Abstract In the context of modern machine learning, models deployed in real-world scenarios often encounter diverse data shifts like covariate and semantic shifts, leading to challenges in both out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization and detection. Despite considerable attention to these issues separately, a unified framework for theoretical understanding and practical usage is lacking.

arxiv-2412-05863.title: Run 3 performance and advances in heavy-flavor jet tagging in CMS
arxiv-2412-05863.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by *. Identification of hadronic jets originating from heavy-flavor quarks is extremely important to several physics analyses in High Energy Physics, such as studies of the properties of the top quark and the Higgs boson, and searches for new physics. Recent algorithms used in the CMS experiment were developed using state-of-the-art machine-learning techniques to distinguish jets emerging from the decay of heavy flavour (charm and bottom) quarks from those arising from light-flavor (udsg) ones.

arxiv-2503-09213.title: JENA White Paper on Software and Heterogeneous Architectures
arxiv-2503-09213.creator: Mohammad Al-Turany, David Chamont, Davide Costanzo, Caterina Doglioni, Håvard Helstrup, Bruno Khélifi, Thomas Kuhr, Paul Laycock, Adrien Matta, Eva Santos, Luis Sarmiento Pico, Fabien Schüssler, Oxana Smirnova, Graeme A Stewart, Gabriel Stoicea, Liliana Teodorescu, Christoph Weniger
arxiv-2503-09213.description: Abstract 1 Executive Summary The scientific communities of nuclear, particle, and astroparticle physics are continuing to advance and are facing unprecedented software challenges due to growing data volumes, complex computing needs, and environmental considerations. As new experiments emerge, software and computing needs must be recognised and integrated early in design phases.

arxiv-2504-00811.title: Passive objects in a chiral active bath: from micro to macro
arxiv-2504-00811.creator: Cory Hargus, Federico Ghimenti, Julien Tailleur, Frédéric van Wijland
arxiv-2504-00811.description: Abstract We present a detailed derivation of the Langevin dynamics obeyed by a massive rigid body immersed in a chiral active bath. We show how the antisymmetric nature of the noise leads to an unusual relationship between the Langevin equation describing stochastic trajectories and the Fokker-Planck equation governing the time-evolution of the probability density.

arxiv-2509-08209.title: Tripartite Entanglement Signal from Multipartite Entanglement of Purification
arxiv-2509-08209.creator: Ning Bao, Keiichiro Furuya, Joydeep Naskar
arxiv-2509-08209.description: Abstract We propose a signal Δ p ( 3 ) \Delta^{(3)}_{p} for genuine tripartite entanglement in finite-dimensional quantum systems and Δ w ( 3 ) \Delta^{(3)}_{w} for holographic systems. We prove that Δ p ( 3 ) \Delta^{(3)}_{p} is non-negative for any tripartite entangled mixed states.

arxiv-2510-10040.title: Pushing the Boundaries in CBRS Band: Robust Radar Detection within High 5G Interference
arxiv-2510-10040.creator: Shafi Ullah Khan 1 , Michel Kulhandjian 2 , Debashri Roy 1
arxiv-2510-10040.description: Abstract Spectrum sharing is a critical strategy for meeting escalating user demands via commercial wireless services, yet its effective regulation and technological enablement, particularly concerning coexistence with incumbent systems, remain significant challenges. Federal organizations have established regulatory frameworks to manage shared commercial use alongside mission-critical operations, such as military communications.

arxiv-2603-01085.title: RECOVERY-INFORMED FORECASTING STRATEGY ENHANCEMENT Journal: Annals of Tourism Research
arxiv-2603-01085.creator: Feng Li, Taozhu Ruan

britannica-1911-lyre-bird.title: Lyre-Bird (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-lyre-bird.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-lyre-bird.description: Article 'Lyre-Bird' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 17), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. tetrachords, eliding one interval in each, for the tetrachord, or series of four notes, was very early adopted as the fundamental principle of Greek music, and its origin in the lyre itself appears sure. The basis of the tetrachord is the employment of the thumb and first three fingers of the left hand to twang as many strings, the little finger not being used on account of natural weakness.

pmc-10546110.title: Factors associated with COVID-19 vaccine uptake in adolescents: a national cross-sectional study, August 2021–January 2022, England
pmc-10546110.creator: Felicity Aiano, Georgina Ireland, Annabel Powell, Colin N J Campbell, Alison Judd, Byron Davies, Anisah Saib, Punam Mangtani, Patrick Nguipdop-Djomo, SIS Study Group, Shamez N Ladhani
pmc-10546110.description: ObjectivesTo assess socioeconomic and geographical factors associated with COVID-19 vaccine uptake in pupils attending state-funded secondary schools in England.DesignCross-sectional observational study.SettingState-funded schools in England.ParticipantsPupils aged 12–17 years attending state-funded schools in England for the academic year 2021/2022.Outcome measuresDemographic, socioeconomic and geographical factors associated with vaccination uptake.

pmc-10720220.title: Cognition and attitudes of hospice care among healthcare providers: a case study of Sichuan Province
pmc-10720220.creator: Meng Ling, Pengru Chen, Qiaoying He, Yi Long, Lei Cheng, Chuan You
pmc-10720220.description: BackgroundUnder the background of the increasing aging population and cancer burden in China, the role of hospice care has become increasingly prominent. The government has paid more attention to the development of hospice care and set up pilot hospitals to promote hospice care. Moreover, healthcare providers play a leading role in hospice care services.

pmc-12398038.title: E2F1-autophagy-ALDH1A1 axis enhances self-renewal and drug resistance of lung cancer stem-like cells in a p53-dependent manner
pmc-12398038.creator: Jingyuan Li, Yiyu Chen, Jianyu Wang, Liyuan Liu, Javeria Qadir, Dan Xie, Xue Wan, Yanan Luo, Jiawen Xian, Ting Ye
pmc-12398038.description: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is a predominant subtype of non-small cell lung adenocarcinoma (NSCLC). It is typically asymptomatic and associated with high mortality rates. Despite recent advancements in screening technologies and therapeutic approaches, its pathogenesis still remains elusive. Therefore, it is imperative to explore new diagnostic markers and therapeutic targets for LUAD management.

pmc-12511628.title: Too much or too little? The trajectory of systemic anti-cancer treatment throughout the last year of life of lung cancer patients in Norway
pmc-12511628.creator: Steinar Solberg, Kathinka Schmidt Slørdahl, Marianne Aanerud, Odd Terje Brustugun, Bjørn Henning Grønberg, Nina Helbekkmo, Åslaug Helland, Yngvar Nilssen
pmc-12511628.description: BackgroundThe use of systemic anti-cancer treatment (SACT) at the end of life (EOL) is controversial. The evidence and detailed description of the dynamics of its use are deficient, especially after the introduction of targeted therapies and immunotherapy.MethodsClinical information about lung cancer patients dying in the years 2020–2023 was extracted from the Cancer Registry of Norway.

pmc-12665059.title: A B3 Domain Transcription Factor NtMAB1 Regulates the Release and Outgrowth of Axillary Buds in Tobacco
pmc-12665059.creator: Luyao Xue, Fei Xia, Wenting Song, Xinru Wu, Xiaoshan Jin, Qun Zhong, Tingting Sun, Changbo Dai, Guanshan Liu, Yuhe Sun, Chunming Liu, Shengjun Li, Xuefeng Yao, Dawei Wang
pmc-12665059.description: The release and outgrowth of axillary buds are essential parts of the process of shoot branching in plants, but knowledge of the underlying regulatory mechanisms remains limited. Analysis of mab1‐D, a tobacco mutant with a greater number of axillary branches, showed that the mutant phenotype resulted from positive modulation of axillary buds release and outgrowth.

pmc-12753475.title: Associations of physical activity and sedentary behavior with insomnia in middle-aged and older adults: a cross-sectional study
pmc-12753475.creator: Yiying Lu, Min Liu, Sijing Chen, Xiujun Liu
pmc-12753475.description: ObjectiveTo explore the relationships between physical activity (PA) and sedentary behavior (SB) levels and insomnia among middle-aged and older adults.MethodsThis cross-sectional study involved 3,752 middle-aged and older adults aged 50 years or older from Wuhan, China. PA and SB levels were assessed via the International Physical Activity Questionnaire (IPAQ)-Short Form. Insomnia severity was evaluated by the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI).

pmc-13145628.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A2468 NORDIC AND BALTIC HEALTHCARE PROFESSIONALS’ PERSPECTIVES ON HOME-BASED STROKE REHABILITATION
pmc-13145628.creator: Ann Marie Hestetun-Mandrup, Lena Rafsten, Agnese Karklina, Luca Oppici, Emilie Simonsen, James Rudd
pmc-13145628.description: Background and aimsTwo-thirds of stroke survivors require additional rehabilitation at home. The home has the potential to offer a rich environment for rehabilitation and recovery following stroke, as Environmental Enrichment research has repeatedly shown. Nevertheless, the successful implementation of home-based rehabilitation remains a challenge in the Nordic and Baltic regions.

pmc-13366647.title: Development and validation of the AI-predictive ParaScout in-vitro diagnostic (IVD) system for the microscopic detection of gastro-intestinal helminths in stool
pmc-13366647.creator: Ihor Feoktistov, Rob Koelewijn, Chris Tieken, Lisette van Lieshout, Serena Slavenburg, Rens Zonneveld, Jaap J. van Hellemond
pmc-13366647.description: The comprehensive method to detect gastro-intestinal infections is still microscopic examination of stool specimens. However, manual microscopic examination is laborious, and its accuracy is highly observer-dependent. Therefore, we have developed a deep-learning approach integrated with a digital microscope scanner to detect gastro-intestinal helminths in digital images, which allows faster and more precise detection of gastro-intestinal helminths.

pmc-13435318.title: Retraction: The long non-coding RNA SNHG5 regulates gefitinib resistance in lung adenocarcinoma cells by targetting miR-377/CASP1 axis
pmc-13435318.creator: ZheXing Wang, LiMing Pan, HaiXiang Yu, Yue Wang

pmc-13490746.title: Clinical significance and outcomes of left-sided gallbladder for cholecystectomy: A retrospective cohort study based on 12-year single-center experience
pmc-13490746.creator: Hong Seok Han, Seung Hwan Lee, Geun Hyeok Yang, Sun-Hyung Joo, Hyun Cheol Kim
pmc-13490746.description: Backgrounds/AimsLeft-sided gallbladder (LSG) is a rare biliary anomaly where the gallbladder (GB) is situated to the left of the ligamentum teres, without situs inversus. Most cases are not preoperatively identified during routine evaluations, which tend to focus more on surgical pathology than detailed anatomical variations. This study investigated the clinical implications of LSG in patients undergoing cholecystectomy.

pmc-13587789.title: Correction: Loss of ErbB3 redirects Integrin β1 from early endosomal recycling to secretion in extracellular vesicles
pmc-13587789.creator: Dorival Mendes Rodrigues-Junior, Ana Rosa Sáez-Ibáñez, Julia M. Scheffler, Takeshi Terabayashi, Nina Daubel, Taija Mäkinen, Olof Idevall-Hagren, Aristidis Moustakas, Ingvar Ferby

Ana Rosa Sáez-Ibáñez: conceptualization, data curation, formal analysis, investigation, and visualization.

pmc-13638720.title: Implementation of a prospective neurosurgical complication registry in routine clinical practice
pmc-13638720.creator: Anja Grimmer, Kristina-Maria Geley-Eder, Petra Böhm, Vanessa Seiter, Baran Atli, Anna Hauser, Kathrin Aufschnaiter-Hiessböck, Tobias Rossmann, Eva Horner, Matthias Gmeiner, Michael Giretzlehner, Andreas Gruber, Maria Gollwitzer
pmc-13638720.description: BackgroundReliable and complete documentation is a prerequisite for quality improvement in neurosurgical care. To strengthen internal process monitoring and reduce variability in documentation practices, our department implemented a structured, web-based neurosurgical complication documentation and quality assurance registry combining automated data imports from the hospital information system with minimal standardized manual inputs.
